subject: Thursday orientation invitation
text:
Hello,

I am writing to invite you, and one friend you trust, to the orientation gathering on Thursday evening at the community room. The session begins at six and usually runs for about ninety minutes. There will be a short introduction, a chance to meet two other families, and a practical walk through the sign-in process. I thought this might be a good low-pressure way for you to see how the program works before your first appointment.

The main practical concern is transportation. The room is on the second floor, and the elevator is not working this month. If stairs are difficult, we can arrange for a staff member to meet you in the lobby and help you move between floors, or you may choose a first-floor alternative in the library annex. Please let me know which option you prefer so we can plan the desk and seating without delay. Your friend does not need to register, but please tell me if they are coming, because the room seats only twelve.

Parking is free on the south side after five, but spaces fill quickly during the evening class, so carpooling would be wise. If you need to cancel, please notify me at least one hour beforehand. If you have any other accessibility needs, I will adjust the plan quietly rather than change the schedule. For the paperwork, bring your own folder if you have one. If you cannot read the printed schedule, bring the phone you normally use and I will email a clear copy. Arrive when you can; punctuality is not the goal.
